breakfast.name: Manakish (Lebanese Za'atar Flatbread)
breakfast.description: Traditional Lebanese flatbread topped with za'atar spice blend and olive oil, creating an aromatic, herbaceous breakfast staple served with bread, lemon, and cucumber yogurt
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, salt, and sugar in large bowl
Add warm milk and olive oil gradually while mixing
Knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic
Cover and let rise in warm place for 1-1.5 hours until doubled
Divide dough into 8 portions and shape into balls
On oiled surface, flatten each ball into 1/4-inch thick round
Mix za'atar with olive oil to create paste-like topping
Spread 2 tbsp za'atar mixture on each dough round
Place on baking sheet and let rise 15-20 minutes
Bake at 425°F for 12-15 minutes until edges are golden brown
Serve warm from oven on wooden boards with lemon wedges and cucumber yogurt
breakfast.notes: Za'atar is vibrant spice blend typically containing dried thyme, sumac, toasted sesame seeds, and oregano
breakfast.fun_fact: Manakish is an anchor of the Lebanese breakfast experience. The dough is similar to pizza dough but the topping is distinctly Middle Eastern
alternatives: Use olive paste instead of za'atar

lunch.name: Fattoush (Lebanese Bread Salad)
lunch.description: Traditional Lebanese salad with fresh vegetables, toasted pita bread and sumac. Quick, refreshing lunch popular throughout Levant
instructions: Cut vegetables into chunks
Break pita bread into bite-sized pieces and toast in 350°F oven for 8-10 minutes
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt and pepper
Toss vegetables and herbs with dressing
Add toasted pita and toss immediately before serving
Sprinkle sumac on top
lunch.notes: Add pita just before serving to keep it crispy. Can prepare vegetables ahead and toast pita separately
lunch.fun_fact: Fattoush means to crush/pound in Arabic, referring to breaking bread into salad

dinner.name: Kibbeh Nayye (Raw Meat and Bulgur Mezze)
dinner.description: Lebanese raw meat dish - Lebanese version of steak tartare
ingredients: 300g lean lamb or veal, finely minced
150g fine dark bulgur wheat, soaked and drained
Salt and black pepper to taste
Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling
instructions: Ensure meat is from a trusted butcher and used immediately
Mix minced meat with soaked bulgur thoroughly
Add minced onion, most of mint, parsley, cumin, allspice, cinnamon, salt and pepper
Knead mixture for 5 minutes until it becomes paste-like
Refrigerate 30 minutes
Shape onto serving platter
Using tip of spoon, create decorative indentations across surface
Garnish with remaining fresh mint
Drizzle generously with olive oil
Serve immediately with pita bread
dinner.notes: Must use only the freshest, finest quality meat
dinner.fun_fact: Kibbeh Nayye is Lebanon's version of steak tartare
